subject: Mythology
title: Mythology in Medicine and Science
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mythology in Medicine and Science.

hook.text: The medical symbol is a snake wrapped around a staff. It comes from Asclepius, the Greek god of healing.

buildup.text: The Achilles tendon, the atlas bone in your neck, and morphine in your cabinet all carry mythological names.

discovery.text: Hygeia gave us 'hygiene.' Panacea gave us 'panacea.' Greek healing gods literally named our medical vocabulary.

twist.text: The caduceus — two snakes on a winged staff — is actually Hermes's symbol, not a medical one. It was adopted by mistake.

climax.text: From DNA's 'Prometheus Project' to the Titan supercomputer, science keeps naming its biggest achievements after myths.

punchline.text: Science names its greatest discoveries after gods because they feel that big.

quiz.question: Why is the caduceus (two snakes with wings) incorrectly used as a medical symbol?
options: It was originally the symbol of Hermes, the messenger god, adopted by mistake
It was redesigned in the 1800s to look more modern
It was always a medical symbol but got its myth association later
